title: The Scientific Literature is Poisonous to LLMs
content_html:
We can think of no corpus of text more toxic to the training of useful LLMs than the 21st century scientific literature. Imagining a two-by-two matrix with the axes honest vs. dishonest and right vs. wrong, the scientific literature is splashed haphazardly across all four boxes. Papers often belong in multiple quadrants at once, and not always because of the contributions of different authors. Even worse, papers in any quadrant might deliberately masquerade as work in any other quadrant. Consider, for example, the ordinary scientist who must dress up an honest experiment in a paper full of superlatives and explain that experiment with an incorrect but popular theory so that she can hope to compete for a journal spot against the fraudster down the hall who is free to make up whatever data is most convenient. The result is a minefield of half-truths, convenient omissions, and outright lies that can’t be distinguished from the innocent facts and findings around them. And we won’t even talk about the writing style.

There’s empirical evidence for the negative effect of the academic literature on LLM performance. In 2024 a research team spanning MIT, Cornell, Carnegie Mellon, Google, and OpenAI examined the effects of removing different text corpora from the training data on the performance of an LLM after training (holding the LLM’s structure constant)1. They found that removing ArXiv, PhilPapers, and NIH ExPorter from the training corpus improved the LLM’s performance at answering academic questions and its average performance across all benchmarks while also making the model less likely to generate toxic output. The study is not conclusive on this point because removing Pubmed reduced model performance somewhat, but the mere fact that LLM performance could be improved by wholesale removal of large sets of scientific articles (pre-slop no less!) is pretty suggestive. We wonder whether this result holds up in 2026, but we’d bet that it does.

Scientific metadata is no help either. Once authorship and citations started being used as a metric, all the signal was gamed out of them. Furthermore, high profile institutions and researchers are not immune to misconduct, nor are any particular fields.

This has important practical consequences for using AI to do science. Human scientists use their informal networks to communicate reputational information, verify work through visits and replication, and generally maintain idiosyncratic personal pictures of what work is reliable and what work matters. Because AI agents do not participate in social relationships they cannot access this social metadata except through humans.

This leaves AI for Science efforts with a strange set of choices. They can either create AI agents that human scientists socialize with, frequently record human scientists in private settings, or create an incentive for scientists to provide a steady stream of gossip. Perhaps one way to bootstrap this effort would be to create AI assistants that allow for more scientific work to be done in informal settings. This would amount to surveillance, but perhaps could be worth it for a big enough improvement in our quality of life.

We write Reinvent Science to broaden the conversation around science and science funding, and we rely on you to help us reach as many readers as possible. Please support our work by subscribing and sharing.

content_html_zh:
我们认为，对于培养有用的法学硕士来说，没有什么文本语料库比 21 世纪的科学文献更有害了。 想象一个二乘二的矩阵，其轴为诚实与不诚实、正确与错误，科学文献随意地分布在所有四个方框中。 论文通常同时属于多个象限，并不总是因为不同作者的贡献。 更糟糕的是，任何象限中的论文都可能故意伪装成任何其他象限中的工作。 例如，想象一下，一位普通科学家必须在一篇充满最高级的论文中粉饰一个诚实的实验，并用一个不正确但流行的理论解释该实验，这样她就可以希望与大厅里的欺诈者竞争期刊席位，而欺诈者可以随意编造任何最方便的数据。 结果是一个充满半真半假、方便遗漏和彻头彻尾谎言的雷区，无法与周围无辜的事实和发现区分开来。 我们甚至不会谈论写作风格。

有经验证据表明学术文献对法学硕士成绩有负面影响。 2024 年，一个由麻省理工学院、康奈尔大学、卡内基梅隆大学、谷歌和 OpenAI 组成的研究团队研究了从训练数据中删除不同文本语料库对法学硕士训练后表现的影响（保持法学硕士的结构不变）1。 他们发现，从训练语料库中删除 ArXiv、PhilPapers 和 NIH ExPorter 提高了法学硕士在回答学术问题方面的表现及其在所有基准上的平均表现，同时也使模型不太可能产生有毒输出。 该研究在这一点上并没有得出结论，因为删除 Pubmed 会在一定程度上降低模型性能，但事实是，LLM 性能可以通过批量删除大量科学文章来提高（预倾斜也不少！） 很有启发性。 我们想知道这个结果在 2026 年是否成立，但我们打赌它会成立。

科学元数据也没有帮助。 一旦作者身份和引用开始被用作衡量标准，所有的信号都被利用了。 此外，知名机构和研究人员也不能免受不当行为的影响，任何特定领域也不能幸免。

这对于使用人工智能进行科学研究具有重要的实际影响。 人类科学家利用他们的非正式网络来交流声誉信息，通过访问和复制来验证工作，并通常对哪些工作是可靠的以及哪些工作重要保持独特的个人形象。 由于人工智能代理不参与社交关系，因此除了通过人类之外，它们无法访问此社交元数据。

这给科学人工智能的努力留下了一系列奇怪的选择。 他们可以创建与人类科学家进行社交的人工智能代理，经常在私人环境中记录人类科学家，或者激励科学家提供源源不断的八卦。 也许引导这一努力的一种方法是创建人工智能助手，允许在非正式环境中完成更多的科学工作。 这相当于监视，但为了我们的生活质量得到足够大的改善，也许这是值得的。

我们撰写《重塑科学》是为了扩大围绕科学和科学资助的对话，我们依靠您来帮助我们吸引尽可能多的读者。 请通过订阅和分享来支持我们的工作。
